content.text: I reviewed every input file, all ten draft sections, the numeral ledger, and all five figure briefs, and traced each claim limitation, numbered part, and figure statement back to the disclosure and the USER passage in the conversation.

input.summary: Full source ledger built and traced. Every limitation of claims 1-17 (apparatus, installed-assembly, and method sets), every one of the 28 entries in draft/numerals.md (10, 12, 14, 16, 18, 20, 22, 24, 26, 30, 32, 34, 36, 38, 40, 42, 44, 46, 48, 50, 52, 54, 56, 58, 60, 62, 64, 66), every structure, relationship, result, position, and variant in the title, field, summary, brief description, detailed description, abstract, and all five figure briefs was checked against the affirmative inventor passages in input/disclosure.md and the single USER passage in input/conversation.md. Result: no unsupported technical matter was found. Each of the following traces to an exact affirmative source passage: semicircular halves, hinge end and latch end ("joined by a hinge at one end and a releasable latch at the other end"); three jaw carriages in radial guides with pivoting concave pads and no tool-specific diameter; segmented cam ring in an annular guide with one segment per frame half; complementary drive faces at the hinge and latch ends coupling the segments on closure; followers in respective oblique slots; wedge driven against a drive face of the cam ring through a limited stroke; synchronized inward travel of all three carriages; outward carriage springs; the holding position and the over-center position; the force-limiting spring stack between latch handle and wedge absorbing travel after all pads contact; the visible indicator pin moving relative to a fixed edge of the latch housing at a predetermined compression range and not measuring diameter; the install and remove sequences; the mounting boss outside the annular guide supporting a sensor, tool, or conduit and not participating in synchronization; and the essential-relationship paragraph. The "installed clamp assembly" statutory class rests on the disclosed clamp gripping a pipe and adds no new structure. Figure-brief geometry was tested against the functional-surface rule: the abutting matching end faces at the two junctions trace to "complementary drive faces ... couple the segments"; the ring drive face near the latch-end junction traces to the wedge being carried by the latch, which sits at the latch end; slot inclination is left unquantified and the shared rotational sense follows from the disclosed synchronized inward travel; the hinge circle, latch rectangle, housing, wedge block, boss projection, and pad blocks are generic outlines expressly marked schematic that add no taper, angle, depth, runout, or contact topology. No "by way of example", "any closed outline", or shape-broadening sentence appears in the application text, and no drafting note, placeholder, open question, or unresolved alternative remains. The agent's own prose in conversation.md about a "self-adhering layer with a microsuction surface" is not inventor support and correctly appears nowhere in the draft. Three internal-consistency defects were verified and are reported: the detailed description cites FIG. 2 for numerals 38 and 40 that are labeled only on FIG. 5; FIG. 5 is never cited anywhere in the detailed description, leaving 26 and 42 introduced under a "Referring to FIG. 2" heading although they are labeled only on FIG. 5; and the FIG. 5 enlarged detail of the jaw carriage omits the pivot mounting that FIG. 2 depicts and that the claims and description require. Each carries a filing-clean automatic fix. Section-line designations were checked: no view is designated a sectional view, so there is no designation to repeat, and numeral-to-part mapping is one-to-one across the ledger, the description, and every sheet.

findings.title: Description cites FIG. 2 for numerals 38 and 40 that appear only on FIG. 5
findings.where: draft/08-detailed-description.md, "The segmented cam ring" section; figures/FIG-2.md numeral list; figures/FIG-5.md
findings.detail: The detailed description states that the follower 40 and the oblique slot 38 are shown in FIG. 2, but the FIG. 2 brief's numeral set is [22, 24, 30, 36, 66]; neither 38 nor 40 is labeled on that sheet. Those two numerals are labeled only on FIG. 5, whose brief targets "38: the slot outline, clear of the follower circle" and "40: the follower circle". A reference-character citation pointing to a sheet where the character does not appear is an internal inconsistency between the description, the numeral ledger, and the figure briefs, and draws an objection under 37 CFR 1.84(p)(5). FIG. 2 does draw an unnumbered follower circle and slot outline, so the geometry is not in conflict; only the citation is wrong.
findings.evidence: Description: "Each jaw carriage 22 carries a follower 40 that is received in a respective oblique slot 38 of the cam ring 30. The follower 40 and the oblique slot 38 are shown in FIG. 2." FIG-2.md: "numerals: [22, 24, 30, 36, 66]" and "Reference numerals appearing on this sheet: 22, 24, 30, 36, 66." FIG-5.md: "numerals: [22, 26, 38, 40, 42]".
findings.fix: In draft/08-detailed-description.md replace the sentence "The follower 40 and the oblique slot 38 are shown in FIG. 2." with "The follower 40 and the oblique slot 38 are shown in FIG. 5." Make no change to any figure brief.

findings.title: FIG. 5 is never referred to in the detailed description, and numerals 26 and 42 are introduced under a FIG. 2 heading
findings.where: draft/08-detailed-description.md, "Jaw carriages and jaw pads" section; draft/07-drawings.md; figures/FIG-5.md
findings.detail: The detailed description refers to FIG. 1, FIG. 2, FIG. 3 and FIG. 4 but never once to FIG. 5, even though FIG. 5 is listed in the Brief Description of the Drawings and is the only sheet on which numerals 26, 38, 40 and 42 are labeled. Numerals 26 (jaw pad) and 42 (carriage spring) are first used in the paragraph block opening "Referring to FIG. 2", implying they are labeled on FIG. 2, where they are not. This leaves one declared view undescribed in the body and mis-associates three numerals with the wrong sheet.
findings.evidence: Brief description: "FIG. 5 is an enlarged detail view of a single jaw carriage, showing the jaw pad, the carriage spring, and the follower that engages an oblique slot in the cam ring." Description: "Referring to FIG. 2, each jaw carriage 22 is slidable in a respective radial guide 24 of the frame. ... Each jaw carriage 22 carries a jaw pad 26 that is mounted on the jaw carriage 22 for pivoting movement ... A carriage spring 42 biases each jaw carriage 22 outward". FIG-2.md numeral list contains neither 26 nor 42; FIG-5.md targets "26: well inside the concave edged pad" and "42: the zigzag spring".
findings.fix: In draft/08-detailed-description.md change the opening of the "Jaw carriages and jaw pads" section from "Referring to FIG. 2, each jaw carriage 22 is slidable" to "Referring to FIGS. 2 and 5, each jaw carriage 22 is slidable", so that the numerals labeled on FIG. 5 (26, 38, 40, 42) are cited to a view on which they appear and every declared view is referred to in the body.

findings.title: FIG. 5 enlarged detail omits the pivot mounting of the jaw pad that FIG. 2 depicts
findings.where: figures/FIG-5.md, "Geometry to draw" bullet 3; compare figures/FIG-2.md, pad bullet
findings.detail: FIG. 5 is the enlarged detail of a single jaw carriage and its jaw pad, yet it specifies the pad only as "a small block with a concave inner edge" attached with no indication of the pivot connection. FIG. 2, the overview, does specify the pivot connection for the same part. The pivoting mounting of the pad on the carriage is a disclosed and claimed relationship, so the detail view and the overview describe the same joint inconsistently, and the sheet that carries numeral 26 is the one that omits it. The fix adds only the connection already disclosed and already depicted on FIG. 2, and asserts no undisclosed geometry.
findings.evidence: FIG-5.md: "On the inner end of the carriage (at the bottom of the drawing area), a pad drawn as a small block with a concave inner edge." FIG-2.md: "On the inner end of each carriage a pad drawn as a small block with a concave inner edge, joined to the carriage at a small circle." Source: "carries a pivoting concave jaw pad that bears on a pipe". Claim 1: "a jaw pad that is mounted on the jaw carriage for pivoting movement".
findings.fix: In figures/FIG-5.md amend the pad bullet to read: "On the inner end of the carriage (at the bottom of the drawing area), a pad drawn as a small block with a concave inner edge, joined to the carriage at a small circle, as in FIG. 2." Leave the existing "The pad, follower, slot, and spring are shown schematically." statement in place and add no other geometry.
